description: Fleet session-management Phase B, D1 (AMEND 5b). Sends '/compact' over the resolved host driver's driver channel (stream-json stdin) to the running Claude Code process behind agent_instance_id -- fire-and-forget, this call does not read or await the resulting turn. Unlike clear_session, compact_session has no park mode and performs no lifecycle_state transition of any kind -- it is pure context hygiene. Only available on hosts whose driver provides a driver channel (currently 'headless' and 'tmux'); the degenerate 'operator' driver, and a headless/tmux process this build's memory no longer tracks (e.g. after a restart), both refuse with unsupported_on_host rather than silently doing nothing.
embedding_description: Trim token bloat on a chatty long-lived fleet session via '/compact' -- the model re-summarizes its own history in place as a digest instead of throwing it away, never touching the lifecycle row. Run this proactively before the context window fills up, not as an emergency reset -- for that, see clear_session. terminate_session is different: it ends the process.

result_processor_customizations.result_description: lifecycle_state -- the row's lifecycle_state at call time, unchanged by this verb (compact_session never transitions state).
result_processor_customizations.presentation_guidance: This call is fire-and-forget: a clean result confirms the command was sent over the driver channel, not that the target session has finished compacting.

error_processor_customizations.action_context: Reads the managed_session ledger row, refuses on a terminal lifecycle_state, resolves the row's host driver, and sends '/compact' over its driver_channel() -- a fixed sequence, no retry loop, no state write.
error_processor_customizations.error_interpretation: session_not_found: no managed_session row exists for the given agent_instance_id. lifecycle_state_conflict: the row is already terminated/retired -- terminal rows never receive driver-channel commands. unsupported_on_host: the row's host has no driver in this build, or its driver has no live driver channel for this host_ref (the degenerate 'operator' driver, or a headless process spawned before a restart wiped this build's in-memory tracking).
error_processor_customizations.recovery_guidance: For unsupported_on_host, use the manual equivalent for that session (e.g. typing /compact directly if it is an operator-attended session) -- this verb has no fallback path, by design, to avoid a silent no-op.
